text.font-family: 'Playfair Display', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', 'Liberation Serif', serif

text.tspan: Multidimensional poverty is defined as being deprived in a range of health, education and living standards
indicators. The MPI is a measure that combines the prevalence and the intensity of multidimensional poverty on
a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher poverty. Estimates based on the most recent household survey

tspan.tspan: Alkire et al. (2026) – The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2026
A separate dataset is produced to monitor trends over time. Where data for 2014 is unavailable, the value from the closest year
